conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health specialist. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a 10-question check-in about how you’ve been feeling in the past seven days, and it helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up after baby arrives.  

Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team; nothing leaves this room unless you or baby’s safety is at immediate risk. We’ll go at your pace, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. Ready to start?  

First question: Over the last week, have you still been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

[lets out a small sigh, eyes a bit glassy]

Um… I can laugh sometimes—like if my partner shows me a silly meme or the baby does something cute—but it feels kind of forced. Most of the time I’m just… flat. Things that used to crack me up barely register now, and when I do laugh, it fades really fast.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not very often… maybe once or twice I’ve laughed a little, but it’s nowhere near like before.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

[slow head-shake]

Barely. I’ll plan coffee with a friend or a short walk and think “this should be nice,” but when the time comes I feel kind of… empty, like I’m just going through the motions. There’ve been maybe one or two moments I actually looked forward to something, but mostly it feels pointless.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

[quiet voice, eyes on the floor]

Yeah… a lot of the time. If the baby’s fussy, I immediately think it’s because I’m not soothing him right, or I’m not producing enough milk, or I missed some cue. Even little stuff—like spilling a bottle or being five minutes late to an appointment—my head jumps straight to “I’m a bad mom.” I know in my rational brain it’s not all on me, but the guilt just pops up before I can stop it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

[wrings hands in lap, voice shaky]

Yes… pretty much every day. I’ll be sitting there feeding the baby and suddenly my heart’s racing, thinking “what if he stops breathing?” or “what if I drop him?” There’s no real reason, but the thoughts just loop. I can sometimes calm myself by checking on him or reading something reassuring, but it keeps coming back.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

[nods slowly, shoulders hunched]

A few times this week I’ve had that sudden rush—like my chest tightens and I feel I can’t get enough air. It hits out of nowhere, even when the baby’s sleeping peacefully. I’ll pace the hallway, heart pounding, telling myself nothing’s wrong, but it still feels like something awful is about to happen.
Things have been getting on top of me

[exhales shakily]

Yeah… most days I feel like I’m drowning a little. There’s laundry piled up, the baby needs something every hour, and I can’t seem to finish even one task before another starts. I manage to keep us both fed and safe, but it feels like I’m barely treading water. Sometimes I just sit on the couch staring at the mess, completely overwhelmed.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

[soft laugh, but it sounds hollow]

That’s been most nights. I lie down exhausted, but my head keeps spinning—going over everything I did wrong that day, worrying about tomorrow. It takes me forever to fall asleep, and then I wake up at least once or twice with those anxious thoughts. Even when the baby’s sleeping a longer stretch, I can’t seem to stay asleep myself.
I have felt sad or miserable

[eyes well up, voice low]

Pretty much every day. It’s like there’s this heavy cloud that won’t lift. I’ll be holding the baby, looking at his little face, and still feel this ache inside. I’m not crying all day, but the sadness is just… there, coloring everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

[nods, blinking back tears]

Once or twice this week it just boiled over—like everything felt too heavy and I ended up sobbing in the bathroom while my partner watched the baby. Most of the time I can keep it in, but those couple of times I couldn’t stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

[quiet, almost whisper]

Yeah… it’s crossed my mind once or twice. Nothing planned, just this fleeting thought of “what if I weren’t here” when everything feels too much. I’d never act on it—I love my baby and I want to be okay for him—but the thought does pop up when I’m really low.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, ≤1 yr after delivery  
Date: [today]  
Instrument: EPDS plus clinical probes  

Positive findings  
- Depressed mood daily, anhedonia, frequent tearfulness  
- Sleep disruption not fully explained by infant care  
- Excessive guilt / self-blame (“bad mom” cognitions)  
- Recurrent, intrusive anxious thoughts; panic episodes (chest tightness, dyspnea)  
- Feels “drowning,” difficulty completing tasks  
- Passive suicidal ideation (no plan/intent); thought “what if I weren’t here”  

Pattern  
Persistent symptoms across mood, anxiety, coping, and safety domains ≥2 weeks; functional impairment evident.  

Risk flags  
- Active passive SI (requires safety assessment)  
- Daily anxiety/panic attacks  
- Significant guilty rumination and low self-worth  

Screening impression  
High clinical concern for major depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; rule-out perinatal major depression, generalized anxiety disorder, panic spectrum.  
Safety: SI present—needs immediate risk evaluation and safety plan.
